sentences.ko: 그래서 내가 지금 이를 그렇게 열심히 관리하는 거야.
sentences.text: That's why I take such good care of my teeth now.

alts.text: So yeah, I'm super careful with my teeth these days.
For that reason, I look after my teeth very carefully now.

sentences.note: **take such good care of** 는 '아주 잘 챙기고 관리한다'는 뜻으로 몸·건강·물건에 두루 씁니다. 왜 그런 습관이 생겼는지 이유를 대며 말할 때 딱 맞고, 격식 있게는 **look after** 로 바꿔 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: I'll bet it went better than you think.

alts.text: Honestly, it probably went way better than you think.
I am quite sure it went better than you expect.

sentences.note: **I'll bet** 은 내기가 아니라 '분명 …일 거야' 하고 상대를 다독일 때 쓰는 말입니다. 면접이나 발표를 망친 것 같다며 풀 죽은 사람에게 그대로 쓸 수 있습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: You walked around all night in the city by yourself.

alts.text: So you were out wandering the city alone all night.
Evidently you were walking around the city alone for the entire night.

sentences.note: **walked around** 는 목적지 없이 여기저기 돌아다녔다는 뜻이고, **by yourself** 는 '혼자서'를 힘주어 말합니다. 상대가 한 일을 놀라거나 걱정하며 되짚을 때 이렇게 그대로 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그러니까 우리 헤어지고 나서 그 책 산 거네?
sentences.text: So, I guess you bought that book after we broke up, huh?

alts.text: You picked up that book after we split, right?
I assume you purchased that book after our relationship ended.

sentences.note: **I guess** 는 확신은 없지만 짐작한 것을 말할 때, 끝에 붙는 **huh** 는 '맞지?' 하고 가볍게 확인할 때 씁니다. 둘을 같이 쓰면 따지지 않고 넌지시 물어보는 말투가 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리 못 알아보실 수도 있어요. 부모님이랑 17년 동안 말도 안 하고 지냈거든요.
sentences.text: You may not recognize us because we haven't spoken to your parents in 17 years.

alts.text: We're probably total strangers to you. Haven't talked to your parents in 17 years.
It is possible that you do not know who we are, as we have not spoken with your parents for 17 years.

sentences.note: **haven't spoken to your parents in 17 years** 처럼 '몇 년째 …을 안 했다'고 할 때는 for 보다 in 을 쓰는 쪽이 훨씬 자연스럽습니다. 오래 연락이 끊긴 사이를 설명할 때 그대로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저는 어릴 때 남들처럼 평범한 엄마 아빠도, 번듯한 가정도 없었어요.
sentences.text: When I was growing up, I didn't have a normal mom and dad or a regular family like everybody else.

alts.text: I didn't grow up with the whole normal mom-and-dad thing everyone else had.
As a child, I did not have the conventional two-parent household that others around me did.

sentences.note: **When I was growing up**은 '어릴 때는'에 해당하는 말로, 자기 어린 시절 이야기를 꺼낼 때 첫머리에 붙입니다. **like everybody else**는 '남들처럼'이라는 뜻으로 문장 끝에 붙여 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: Oh, please, that is such a lame excuse.

alts.text: Come on, that's the lamest excuse ever.
I am afraid that is a rather poor excuse.

sentences.note: **Oh, please**는 상대 말을 못 믿겠다고 받아치는 반응입니다. **such a lame excuse**는 핑계가 성의 없고 뻔할 때 쓰는데, 친한 사이에서 가볍게 놀리는 자리에 어울립니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.text: You're more than welcome to come with us, right?

alts.text: Feel free to tag along, yeah?
We would be very glad to have you join us.

sentences.note: **more than welcome to**는 그냥 '괜찮다'보다 훨씬 적극적으로 권하는 말입니다. 상대가 끼어도 되나 눈치를 볼 때, 부담 갖지 말라는 뜻으로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 야, 그거 진짜 하나도 안 재밌는 게임이잖아.
sentences.text: Okay, that's like the least fun game ever.

alts.text: Man, that game sounds so boring.
I must say, that sounds like a rather tedious game.

sentences.note: **the least fun game ever**처럼 least를 쓰면 '제일 안 ~한'이 됩니다. 한국 사람은 not fun만 떠올리기 쉬운데, 원어민은 이렇게 최상급으로 비꼬듯 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그거 하나 때문에 테이블도 닦고 우유도 데웠는데, 진짜 그럴 가치가 하나도 없었어.
sentences.text: I wiped tables for it, I steamed milk for it, and it was totally not worth it.

alts.text: All that table wiping and milk steaming, and it wasn't even worth it.
Despite all the tables I cleaned and the drinks I prepared, it did not prove worthwhile.

sentences.note: **totally not worth it**은 고생한 만큼 값을 못 했다고 할 때 씁니다. 물건을 샀을 때도, 일을 했을 때도 똑같이 쓸 수 있는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends
